PullRequest.Title: smoke: keep a Chromium network log when the Windows web workbench does not restore
PullRequest.Body:
Diagnostics for `SMOKE-WEB-WORKBENCH-NOT-READY`, a Windows browser smoke flake in the merge queue (runs [43956914777](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/43956914777) and [43982200585](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/43982200585)). Test-only.

## What fails

In both runs, a late suite (8 or 9) starts a fresh server, which prints `Server bound to ::1:900x (IPv6)`. During `page.goto()`, exactly one workbench module request fails with `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`:

- `http://localhost:9007/oss-dev/static/out/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalTabbedView.js`
- `http://localhost:9008/oss-dev/static/out/vs/workbench/contrib/share/common/share.js`

The broken import stops the workbench from booting, so `Application#checkWindowReady` times out on `.monaco-workbench` after 20 s. The server was alive the whole time. It logged no errors and only exited at teardown.

That makes 2 of the 59 Windows browser smoke runs in the 8 h I scanned (about 530 workbench loads). No other run had a refused request.

## Why we need more data

Chromium resolves `localhost` to `[::1, 127.0.0.1]` and connects with `TransportConnectJob`, since HappyEyeballsV3 is off by default. It tries `::1` first and falls back to `127.0.0.1` when `::1` fails or takes longer than 300 ms. When both fail, it reports the last error. So a final `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` means the `::1` connect itself failed, and the refused IPv4 fallback hides its real error and timing.

I couldn't reproduce it locally:
- 40 loads of the real dev server with a fresh server per load, under 31 cores of CPU load: no failures and no IPv4 attempts.
- A netlog shows only about 8 `::1` connects per workbench load, each under 3 ms.
- Windows refuses connects once a listener's backlog fills (about 232 pending with Node defaults), but Chromium opens far too few sockets to get there.

Changing the binding (for example `--host 127.0.0.1`) would be a guess, and it would change smoke behavior on every platform. So this records the network log that tells us what happened.

## Change

- **Windows Chromium only:** `launchBrowser` passes `--log-net-log=<tmp>` with `--net-log-max-size-mb=200`. The raw log is written outside `.build/logs`, so it never gets uploaded as is. A workbench load logs about 80 MB.
- **Keep it only on failure:** after `playwright.close()` (Chromium writes the log on close), `PlaywrightDriver.close` gzips it to `<suite logs>/chromium-netlog.json.gz` if `whenWorkbenchRestored()` never succeeded. It deletes the raw log either way.
- **Navigation failure:** if `page.goto()` itself rejects, `launchBrowser` closes Chromium, keeps the log the same way, and rethrows.
- Passing suites keep nothing. A failing suite adds about 2–4 MB to the logs artifact.

## Validation

I drove `launch()` from `test/automation` against the dev server, with headless Chromium on Windows:
- **Restored workbench:** no `.gz`, and the raw log was deleted.
- **`share.js` aborted with `connectionrefused`:** this reproduces the exact CI log line. The workbench didn't restore, a 2.0 MB `chromium-netlog.json.gz` was kept (about 267k events, valid JSON), and the raw log was deleted.
- **Main document aborted with `connectionrefused`:** `launch()` rethrew `page.goto: net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`, the `.gz` was kept, and no raw log was left.
- `tsc` on `test/automation` and `oxlint` on the changed files are clean.

> Authored with Copilot

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful Windows Chromium web smoke suite, including workbench restoration and normal teardown
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Application.start awaits server startup, browser launch, navigation, workbench DOM readiness, and the existing restoration RPC. Network logging runs during the browser lifetime. On stop, driver.close closes the browser, deletes the raw log, and tears down the server; Code.exit polls for server termination rather than directly awaiting driver.close.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn the workbench server and launch the selected browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server and browser per application launch, as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subprocess launches occurred without Chromium NetLog arguments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both must start before navigation; only browser launch arguments change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate to the existing server endpoint and fetch workbench resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing page/resource request count; no new application network requests are added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same navigation and workbench resource loading occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Navigation and module loading precede readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Record Chromium network events to a temporary file, finish logging when closing, and remove the raw log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One raw log per browser, configured with a 200 MB limit; one removal on normal close. No successful-run compression or artifact copy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No NetLog file was recorded, flushed, or deleted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Recording adds diagnostic I/O during the suite; close/delete precede server teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the window driver, await restoration, extract existing client logs, and close the browser.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Restoration retains the same evaluateHandle/evaluate calls per polling attempt. Client log extraction and browser close remain once per normal teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls; the PR only records successful restoration in a boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restoration gates startup; log extraction and close precede server termination.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read existing client logs, write their copies, and terminate the server process tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing reads/writes scale with client log files; one teardown with its existing retry policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same client log copying and server termination occurred without intervening NetLog cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These remain on shutdown; raw-log deletion is inserted before server teardown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One browser and raw log per suite/application launch, not one per module request. Event production scales with network activity; the launch requests a 200 MB log limit. The source comment estimates about 80 MB per workbench load, but this was not independently measured.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The inspected suite hooks await application startup and shutdown. Logging is browser-owned; normal teardown does not start compression. No new per-request subprocess or Playwright RPC fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Every browser launch has a PID/counter-specific log path and a fresh restoration boolean. Logging is not skipped for warm network caches, although reduced network activity can reduce events. Successful restoration causes deletion without reading or gzipping the log.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the platform gate, one-log-per-browser ownership, unchanged RPC/request multiplicity, success-path deletion, and configured size limit, directly from the changed code and callers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual NetLog generation rate, Chromium limit implementation, disk throughput, and startup overhead are not measured by the supplied repository evidence.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance bug established. The new bounded diagnostic recording is intentional; successful runs do not additionally read, compress, or retain the raw data. No independent repeated-work or fan-out regression was found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigation succeeds but the workbench never restores; suite teardown preserves diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Application.checkWindowReady fails before successful restoration. The registered Code instance is stopped by the suite after hook. Driver.close performs existing client-log extraction and browser close, then awaits NetLog compression/removal before terminating the server. Code.exit retains its existing server polling and force-kill fallback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract existing web client logs and close Chromium before consuming its network log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same existing teardown calls once per driver close.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same calls were followed directly by server teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: They precede the newly added compression step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the suite log directory, stream the raw NetLog through gzip to chromium-netlog.json.gz, and delete the raw file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory creation, streaming input/output pair, and removal per failed browser; O(raw log bytes) compression with stream backpressure rather than whole-file buffering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No network-log read, gzip work, artifact write, or deletion occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after Chromium closes and before the normal server teardown; it does not block a successful workbench becoming usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Terminate the server with existing tree-kill logic and existing forced-exit fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normal teardown plus the pre-existing fallback if shutdown exceeds its threshold; no new subprocess loop is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normal server termination followed browser close without NetLog processing; the same timeout fallback existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal termination now follows diagnostic compression; existing Code.exit can terminate the server independently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One retained log per failed browser startup, not per refused request or readiness polling attempt. Compression work scales with the closed browser's raw log size, configured to at most 200 MB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One backpressured read-to-gzip-to-write pipeline per failed browser. The pipeline is awaited within driver.close; there is no Promise.all over network events or log chunks. Existing Code.exit can force server termination after roughly ten seconds independently of completion of close.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No shared cache or retained map is introduced. A false restoration boolean selects preservation; normal helper completion or stream failure runs raw-file removal in finally. Repeated launches receive different raw paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that preservation is once per failed browser and compression is streamed, failure-only, and ordered after browser close. Its placement before server teardown is explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency, compression duration, compressed size, and interaction with unusually slow storage are unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression beyond the intended failure-diagnostic cost. There is no evidence of unbounded in-memory buffering, per-event compression, uncontrolled concurrency, or newly introduced persistent resource loss. This PR adds diagnostics rather than fixing the underlying connection failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Windows Chromium page.goto rejects before a PlaywrightDriver is returned
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The launchBrowser catch now awaits browser.close and preservation/removal of the NetLog, then rethrows the navigation error. No driver is constructed for this branch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close the already-launched Chromium browser when navigation rejects.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One close attempt per rejected Windows Chromium navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The rejected navigation propagated without this local browser-close attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: New cleanup is awaited before the original error is rethrown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stream the closed browser's raw NetLog into a gzip artifact and remove the raw file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pipeline and deletion per failed launch, not per failed network request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no NetLog preservation or removal before propagating the navigation failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds diagnostic time to the already-failing launch path, not the successful startup path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One browser close and one preservation pipeline per rejected navigation. Cost scales with the events captured before failure, subject to the configured browser log limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser closure and the single streaming gzip pipeline run sequentially. There is no retry or per-module fan-out in the added catch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The unique raw path is consumed once and removed in the helper's finally block. This path always preserves diagnostics regardless of cache warmth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in branch reachability, sequential scheduling, and bounded streaming allocation from the catch and shared helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of events preceding navigation rejection and resulting compression delay are not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. Added work is explicit failure cleanup and diagnostic preservation. The pre-existing server-registration gap on launch failure is not caused by this diff and is not reported.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron, non-Windows web browsers, and Windows Firefox/WebKit smoke runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing startup, restoration, and shutdown paths remain in place. The restoration wrapper sets one boolean after the existing awaited window-driver operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the existing restoration evaluation and normal application shutdown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged call count per restoration attempt and close.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC and shutdown operations occurred without setting the local restoration boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No additional expensive boundary is inserted; NetLog handling is skipped because netLogPath is undefined.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional boolean per PlaywrightDriver and constant local work per successful restoration call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new tasks, subprocess launches, or collection traversal on these gated-out paths.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No NetLog path is allocated and no new cache exists. Existing browser and driver behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the process.platform/browserType gate and optional constructor parameter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material performance magnitude uncertainty: the added local state and assignment are constant-sized.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both changed files and every diff page in the performance-review pass. Traced startup, restoration polling, suite ownership, normal shutdown, failed restoration, and navigation rejection. Evaluated diagnostic I/O, streaming allocation, cleanup, effective boundary cardinality, and concurrency. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bug or qualifying regression fix was established; no findings submitted.
